validated_results.title: Alcohol consumption and risk of prostate cancer in middle-aged men.
validated_results.reason: Original population-based case-control study of alcohol (including red wine) consumption and newly diagnosed prostate cancer, providing a risk estimate for incident disease.

extraction.comparison_type: Each additional glass of red wine consumed per week (continuous)
extraction.population: Middle-aged men aged 40-64 years, newly diagnosed prostate cancer cases and age-frequency-matched population controls

cases.excerpt: A total of 753 newly diagnosed prostate cancer cases, 40-64 years of age, participated in the study.

effect_size.excerpt: Each additional glass of red wine consumed per week showed a statistically significant 6% decrease in relative risk (OR = 0.94; 95% CI = 0.90-0.98), and there was evidence for a decline in risk estimates across increasing categories of red wine intake (trend p = 0.02).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Each additional glass of red wine consumed per week showed a statistically significant 6% decrease in relative risk (OR = 0.94; 95% CI = 0.90-0.98), and there was evidence for a decline in risk estimates across increasing categories of red wine intake (trend p = 0.02).

comparison.excerpt: Each additional glass of red wine consumed per week

design.excerpt: Data from a population-based case-control study in King County, WA, were utilized

timing.excerpt: All participants completed an in-person interview on lifetime alcohol consumption and other risk factors for prostate cancer.

continent.excerpt: population-based case-control study in King County, WA

exposure_measurement.excerpt: All participants completed an in-person interview on lifetime alcohol consumption

validated_results.reason: The "valine" exposure is the HER-2 codon 655 Ile/Val genetic polymorphism rather than a nutritional valine exposure.

validated_results.reason: The "arginine" exposure is the FGFR-4 Arg388 germline allele, a genetic variant rather than nutritional arginine intake or status.

validated_results.title: Green tea constituent epigallocatechin-3-gallate selectively inhibits COX-2 without affecting COX-1 expression in human prostate carcinoma cells.
validated_results.reason: The study of green tea constituent EGCG on COX-2 expression was conducted exclusively in LNCaP and PC-3 human prostate carcinoma cell lines with no human incidence data.

validated_results.reason: This is a preclinical cell-line experiment on the tea polyphenol EGCG in prostate carcinoma cells, not a human study of tea intake and prostate cancer incidence.
